angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 226,798 km at 22.45 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 44.5348 +/- 0.0381 mas (same row, RUWE 1.86): 22.45 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.326 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Parc et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4336 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..81P/abstract): 226,798 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.306 +/- 0.008 solar masses from Parc et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4336 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..81P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3307 +/- 94 K from Parc et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4336 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..81P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Parc et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4336 A c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..81P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4336-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.897, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
